items.stem: A generalized inverse G of A satisfies:
items.explanation: The first generalized-inverse identity is AGA=A. It ensures that applying A, then G, then A reproduces the action of A.

items.explanation: Reflexivity adds the second identity GAG=G.

items.stem: If A has full column rank, A⁺ equals:
items.explanation: When A has full column rank, its columns are independent, so AᵀA is nonsingular. This permits the left-inverse expression (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ.

items.stem: If A has full row rank, A⁺ equals:
items.explanation: When A has full row rank, its rows are independent, so AAᵀ is nonsingular. The Moore–Penrose inverse is Aᵀ(AAᵀ)⁻¹.

items.stem: The matrix AA⁺ is the orthogonal projection onto:
items.explanation: AA⁺ is symmetric and idempotent, and its column space equals Col(A). Therefore it is the orthogonal projection onto the column space.

items.stem: The matrix A⁺A is the orthogonal projection onto:
items.explanation: A⁺A is symmetric and idempotent, and its column space is Row(A). It projects onto the row space in the domain of A.
